rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory and conquest may be understood generically, encompassing Mecca and other instances; their coming means their actual attainment.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد جنس نصر الله تعالى لرسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام والمؤمنين وجنس الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the coming of victory as its attainment is literal according to al-Raghib; al-Qadi calls it metaphorical.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلام الراغب وقال القاضى مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in “you saw” is apparently to the Prophet, and seeing may be visual or cognitive, the latter taking two objects.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في رأيت للنبى عليه الصلاة والسلام وارؤية بصرية أوعلمية متعدية لمفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The people” means the Arabs, and God’s religion is Islam, the only religion attributed to God.
rows.anchor: والناس والعرب ودين الله ملة الاسلام اتى لادين له تعالى يضاف اليه غيرها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a fawj as a rapidly moving group; elsewhere it means a group generally.
rows.anchor: والافواج جمع فوج وهوعلى ماقال الراغب

rows.speaker: الحوفى
rows.claim: Al-Hufi says the expected plural is afwuj, altered to afwaj because the waw’s damma was heavy.
rows.anchor: قال الحوفى وقياس جمعه أفوج ولكن أستثقلت الضمة على الواو فعدل إلى أفواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bahr notes the plural pattern: sound-root faʿl normally takes afʿul, while hollow-root words normally take afʿāl, with exceptions.
rows.anchor: وفى البحلر قياس فعل صحيح العين أن يجمع على أفعل لاعلى أفعال ومعتل العين بالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwājan is an accusative circumstantial from the subject of “enter”; the clause is circumstantial to “people” on visual seeing, or a second object on cognitive seeing.
rows.anchor: ونصب أفواجا على الحال من الضمير يدخلون وأما جملة يدخلون فهى حال من الناس على الاحتمال الاول

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats “you saw” as “you knew,” allowing “entering” to be a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: بجعل رلأيت بمعنى عرفت كما قال الزمخشرى

rows.speaker: أبوحيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that the proposed sense “you knew” needs substantiation because “saw” is not established as “knew.”
rows.anchor: تعقبه أبوحيان بقوله لانعام أن رأيت جاءت بمعنى عرفت فيحتاج فى ذلك إلى استثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mass entry was the conversion of many groups without fighting between the conquest of Mecca and the Prophet’s death; beforehand people converted individually or in pairs.
rows.anchor: والمراد بدخول الناس في دينه تعالى أفواجا أى جماعات كثيرة اسلامهم من غير قتال وقد كان ذلك بين فتح مكة وموته

rows.speaker: عمرو بن سلمة
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says tribes hurried to profess Islam after the conquest, while some Arab clans had waited to see whether the Prophet prevailed.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخارى عن عمرو بن سلمة قال لما كان الفتح بادر كل قوم باسلامهم إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that after Mecca’s conquest, Arab tribes concluded that one protected from the People of the Elephant could not be resisted, and entered Islam in groups.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن قال لما فتح رسول الله صلى الله تعالى علسه وسلم مكة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says no Arab remained an unbeliever after Hunayn and Taif; some came themselves and others sent delegates.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمر بن عبد البر لم يتوقف رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفى العرب رجل كافر بل دخل الكل فى الاسلام بعد حنين والطائف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya limits “the people” to Arab idolaters, excluding Christian Taghlib, who did not convert in the Prophet’s lifetime but paid jizya.
rows.anchor: وتأول ذلك ابن عطية فقال المراد والله تعالى أعلم العرب عبدة الاوثان فان نصارى بنى تغلب ماأراهم الله أسلموا

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil identify the people as Yemenis; seven hundred reportedly arrived as a delegation and converted.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومقاتل المراد بالناس أهل اليمن وفد منهم سبعمائة رجل وأسلموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas describes the arrival of Yemenis, praising their tender hearts, obedience, faith, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: بما أخرجه ابن جرير من طريق الحصين بن عيسى عن معمر الزهرى عن أبى حازم عن أبى عباس قال بينما رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying that faith and wisdom are Yemeni is reported by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: الايمان يمان جاء في حديث أخرجه البخارى ومسلم والترمذى عن أبى هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying “faith is Yemeni” is explained either by Mecca being Yemeni, the Prophet’s birthplace and source of Islam, or as praise of the Ansar, who were Yemenite.
rows.anchor: فقيل قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لان مكة يمانية ومنها بعث صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفشأ الايمان وقيل ارادة عليه الصلاة والسلام مدح الانصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the report’s Medina setting conflicts with claims that the saying was made at Tabuk, it may have been repeated; it praises Yemenis for accepting faith swiftly without arms and includes the Ansar.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل تكرر القول والظاهر انه ثناء على أهل اليمن لاسراعهم إلى الايمان وقبولهم له بلا سيف

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Issam al-Din suggests “you saw” addresses every believer, and proposes that “the opening” means the opening of the door of religion to people; the author dismisses both suggestions.
rows.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن يكون الخطاب في رأيت الناس عاما لكل مؤمن ثم قال ومما يختلج في القلب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have read the opening as “when God’s opening and victory came,” reversing their order.
rows.anchor: وقرأابن عباس كما اخرج أبو عبيدة وابن المنذر عنه اذاء جاء فتح الله والنصر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, in one transmission, reads “they are entered” in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرا ابن كثير في رواية يدخلون بالبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to glorify God through all remembrance that signifies transcendence, while praising Him for His abundant favor and increasing worship.
rows.anchor: اى فنزهه تعالى بكل ذكر يدل عالى التنزيه حامدا له جلا وعلا زيادة في عبادته والثناء عيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih means declaring God transcendent, not merely uttering the formula “subhan Allah”; the preposition denotes accompaniment and the phrase is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: فالتسبيح التنزيه لا التلفظ بكلمة سبحان الله والباء للملابسة والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase combines declaring God free of deficiencies with affirming His perfection and praising Him for His immense favor to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وامعنى على الجمع بين تسبيحه تعالى وهو تنزيه سبحانه عما لايليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says to praise God for delaying victory as a wise timing rather than incapacity; the author calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل أي نزهه تعالى عن العجز في تأخير ظهور الفتح واحمده على التأخير وصفه تعالى بان توقيت الامور من عنده

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In the Two Sahih collections, Aisha reports that the Prophet often said the glorification and forgiveness formula in bowing and prostration, interpreting the Quran.
rows.anchor: ايد ذلك بما في الصحيحين عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يكثر ان يقول في ركوعه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports in Ahmad and Muslim that near the end of his life the Prophet often praised God, sought forgiveness, and repented after being told he would see a sign among his community.
rows.anchor: وكذا كما في مسند الامام أحمد وصحيح ومسلم عن عائشة أيضا قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يكثر في آخر أمره

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits through al-Shabi a rare report from Umm Salama that the Prophet repeated this glorification in all activities at the end of his life and recited the surah.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جرير من طريق حفص ابن عاصم عن الشعبى عن أم سلمة قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في آخر أمره

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report in the Musnad says that after this surah was revealed, the Prophet repeated its glorification and forgiveness wording three times when reciting it and bowing.
rows.anchor: وفي المسند عن أبي عبيدة عن عبد الله بن مسعود لما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم اذا جاء نصر الله والفتح

rows.speaker: ابن رجب
rows.claim: An alternative makes the preposition instrumental and “praise” an agent noun: glorify God by the praise He used for Himself; Ibn Rajab cautions that not every glorification is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الباء للاستعانة والحمد مضاف إلى الفاعل أى سبحه بما حمد سبحانه به نفسه قال ابن رجب اذ ليس كل تسبيح بمحمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense remains accompaniment; Mu'tazilite glorification can deny many divine attributes, as illustrated by Bishr al-Marisi’s abhorrent phrase.
rows.anchor: والظاهر الملابسة وجوز ان يكن التسبيح مجازا عن التعجب بعلاقة السببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats glorification as astonishment at an extraordinary victory and thanks God; Ibn al-Munir objects to turning a command into a report, while the author says commanded reflective gratitude is possible.
rows.anchor: فأن رأى أمرا عجيبا قال سبحان الله أى فتعجب لتيسير الله تعالى بما لم يخطر ببالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors preparing to meet God after completing the mission, since the reports do not support the astonishment reading.
rows.anchor: والاخبار دالة على ان ذلك أمر له صلى اله تعالى عليه وسلم بالاستعداد للتوجه إلى ربه تعالى والاستعداد للقائه

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزى
rows.claim: Al-Jawzi transmits from Ibn Abbas that glorification means prayer, because prayer contains it; the Prophet prayed eight rakas in Umm Hani’s house upon entering Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالتسبيح الصلاة لاشتمالها عليه ونقله ابن الجوزى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That prayer is called the conquest prayer, also performed by Sa'd at Mada'in; proposals of four conquest rakas plus four forenoon rakas also exist, but neither prayer reports establish that tasbih means prayer.
rows.anchor: فهى صلاة الفتح وهى سنة قد صلاها سعد يوم الفتح المدائن وقيل صلاة الضحى وقيل أرع منها للفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported reasons for the Prophet’s seeking forgiveness include continual spiritual ascent, shortcomings relative to his rank, forgetfulness, teaching his community, and seeking forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: واستغفاره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قيل لانه كان دائما في الترقى فاذا ترقى إلى مرتبة استغفر لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be general: the Prophet is included by representative generalization while the command to seek forgiveness applies to others; the author says this is far from the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون الخطاب في رأيت عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone falls short in fulfilling God’s rights; greater knowledge of God brings greater fear and clearer recognition of one’s shortcomings.
rows.anchor: ان كل أحد مقصر عن القيام بحقوق الله تعالى كما ينبغى وادائها على الوجه اللائق بجلاله

rows.speaker: كهمس
rows.claim: Kahmas reportedly prayed a thousand rakas, then rebuked himself as displeasing God even for an instant.
rows.anchor: وقد كان كهمس يصلى كل ألف ركعة فاذا صلى اخذ بلحيته ثم يقول لنفسه قومى ياماؤى كل سوء

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says he wished to be carried to God like a runaway slave, admitting he had never pleased God with himself.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار لقد هممت ان اوصى اذا مت ان ينطلق بي كما ينطلق بالعبد الآبق إلى سيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sought forgiveness because even the greatest worship falls short of what divine majesty deserves; he is authentically reported to seek forgiveness over seventy times daily.
rows.anchor: فيستحى ويهرع إلى الاستغفار وقد صح انه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يستغر الله فى اليوم والليلة اكثر من سبعين مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness is prescribed after many acts of worship: after obligatory prayers, night exertion, pilgrimage, ablution, and gatherings.
rows.anchor: شرع الاستغفار بعد كثير من الطاعات فذكروا انه يشرع لمصلى المكتوبة ان يستغفر عقبها ثلاثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrims are told to seek forgiveness after departing from their ritual gathering, citing the Quran.
rows.anchor: وللحاج ان يستغفر بعد الحج فقد قال تعالى ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس واستغفروا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s supplication upon rising from an assembly models seeking forgiveness at the end of every gathering.
rows.anchor: وقد كان صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول اذا قام من المجلس سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك أستغفرك وأتوب اليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some see the forgiveness command as an allusion to the Prophet’s approaching death; the well-known view is that it signals completion of the mission and religion.
rows.anchor: رمز من هذا الوجه على ماقيل إلى مافهم من النعى والمشهور أن ذلك للدلالة على مشارفة تمام أمر الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of glorification and praise before seeking forgiveness is read as turning first to the Creator’s majesty, then to the servant’s shortcomings; it may also teach supplicants to praise before asking.
rows.anchor: تقديم التسبيح ثم الحمد على الاستغفار قيل على طريقة النزول من الخالق إلى الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is ever accepting repentance” means God has always received penitents’ repentance abundantly, encouraging the repentant to expect acceptance.
rows.anchor: أى منذ خلق المكلفين أى مبالغا فى قبول توبتهم فليكن المستغفر التائب متوقعا للقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing “accepting repentance” instead of “forgiving” signals that seeking forgiveness benefits only when accompanied by repentance.
rows.anchor: واختيار توابا على غفارا مع انه الذى يستدعيه استغفره ظاهرا للتنبيه كما قال بعض الاجلة

rows.speaker: ابن رجب
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab distinguishes unqualified seeking forgiveness, which includes repentance and a request, from the paired formula, which requests forgiveness alone unless accompanied by remorse.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن رجب ان الاستغفار المجرد هو التوبة مع طلب المغفرة بالدعاء والمقرون فاستغفر الله تعالى وأتوب اليه سبحانه هو طلب المغفرة بالدعاء فقط

rows.speaker: ابن رجب
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab says unqualified forgiveness-seeking asks protection from past sin through prayer and remorse and from future sin through resolve; persistence blocks its benefit.
rows.anchor: أن المجرد طلب وقاية شر الذنب الماضى بالدعاء والندم عليه ووقاية شر الذنب المتوقع بالعزم على الاقلاع عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bare request without remorse is mere supplication and apparently unacceptable, with poor manners toward God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر ان ذلك الدعاء المحض غير مقبول وفيه سوء من الادب مع الله تعالى مافيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One scholar sees ellipsis by reciprocal omission: “seek His forgiveness; He is Forgiving,” and “repent to Him; He is ever-accepting.”
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الافاضيل ان فى الآية احتباكا والاصل واستغفره انه كان غفارا وتب اليه انه كان توابا

rows.speaker: الماتريدى
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi says God has eternally been accepting repentance, rather than acquiring this attribute after creating penitents, as the Mu'tazilites say.
rows.anchor: وقال الماتريدى فلى التأويلات أى لم يزل توابا لا أنه سبحانه تواب لاأنه سبحانه تواب بأمر أكتسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that acceptance is a relational attribute and therefore temporally arises is answered by some; others prefer al-Maturidi’s view as affirming an eternal readiness to accept repentance and strengthening hope.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه بان قبول التوبة من الصفات الاضافية ولانزاع فى حدوثها واختار بعضهم ماذهب اليه الماتريدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report promises that if people did not sin, God would replace them with people who sin and seek forgiveness, whom He would forgive.
rows.anchor: وصح لو لم تذنبوا لذهب الله تعالى بكم ولجاء بقوم يذنبون ثم يستغفرون فيغفر لهم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits from Abu Sa'id that saying a bedtime forgiveness formula brings forgiveness even for sins as numerous as sea foam, sand, or leaves.
rows.anchor: أخرج الامام أحمد من حديث حديث عطية عن أبى سعيد مرفوعا من قال حين يأوى إلى فراشه استغفر اله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits from Ibn Abbas that frequent seeking of forgiveness brings relief from every anxiety.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أيضا من حديث ابن عباس من أكثر من الاستغفار جعل الله له من كل هم فرجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Masad is Meccan and has five verses by unanimous agreement.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة المسد وهي مكية وآيها خمس بلا خلاف فى الامرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account links the surah to the previous one by following the mass conversion with the ruin of those who did not join Islam, bringing joy to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبل دخول الناس فى ملة الاسلام عقبه سبحانه بذكر هلاك بعض ممن لم يدخل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account sees threat following promise and joy for the Prophet; the Imam connects the previous “your religion and mine” with promised victory for the Prophet and ruin for his uncle.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من اتصال الوعيد بالوعد وفى كل مسرة له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال الامام في ذلك انه تعالى لما قال لكم دينكم

rows.speaker: الامام
rows.claim: The Imam says victory is the reward of the obedient while worldly loss and afterlife punishment answer the question about the disobedient; he calls the surah arrangement striking despite their distant revelation dates.
rows.anchor: فكانه قيل الهى ما جزاء المطيع قال حصول النصر والفتح ثم قيل فما جزاء العاصى قال الخسار فى الدنيا والعقاب فى العقبى

rows.speaker: جبير
rows.claim: Jubayr and others explain “tabbat” as perished, comparable to the expression for an old woman ruined by age.
rows.anchor: أى هلكت كما قال جبير وغيره ومنه قولهم أشابة أم تابة يريدون أم هالكة من الهرم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Qatada explain the word as loss; Ibn Abbas also glosses it as failure.
rows.anchor: والتعجيز أى خسرت كما قال ابن عباس وابن عمر وقتادة وعن الاول أيضا خابت

rows.speaker: يمان بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yaman ibn Waththab interprets the word as becoming empty of every good; the reported glosses are close in sense.
rows.anchor: وعن يمان بن وثاب صفرت من كل خير وهى على مافى فى البحر أقوال متقاربة

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab traces the root to cutting, which leads to destruction; al-Raghib calls it continued loss.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب ان مادة التباب تدور على القطع وهو مؤد إلى الهلاك ولذا فسر به وقال الراغب هو الاستمرار فى الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab was Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet’s uncle and a fierce opponent.
rows.anchor: هو عبد العزى عبد المطلب عم رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وكان شديد المعاداة والمناصبة له

rows.speaker: طارق المحاربى
rows.claim: A report from Tariq al-Muharibi recounts Abu Lahab following the young Prophet through Dhul-Majaz, throwing stones until his legs bled and calling him a liar.
rows.anchor: فى المجمع عن طارق المحاربى قال بينا أنا بسوق ذى المجاز اذا أنا برجل حديث السن يقول أيها الناس قولوا لااله الا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in the Two Sahihs and al-Tirmidhi says that when 26:214 was revealed, the Prophet called Quraysh from Safa, warned them of imminent punishment, and Abu Lahab cursed him, prompting this surah.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الامام أحمد والشيخان والترمذى عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت وأنذر عشيرتك الاقربين صعد النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على الصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version says Abu Lahab raised a stone to throw at the Prophet; the reports explain why the verse singles out his hands.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنه مع ذلك القول أخذ بيديه حجرا ليرمى بها رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عيه وسلم ومن هذا يعلم وجه ايثار التباب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits Ibn Abbas’s account that after leaving the ravine, Abu Lahab mocked the promised afterlife, inspected and blew on his hands, and cursed them; the surah was then revealed.
rows.anchor: وكذا مما روى البيهقى فى الدلائل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tariq’s report particularly explains the reference to the two hands, which may be literal; the whole utterance curses both hands and the person.
rows.anchor: ومما روى عن طارق يعلم وجه الثانى فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses may instead state as fact that both his hands and he himself perished; the past tense marks certain fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وجوز ان يكونا اخبارين بهلاك ذينك الامرين والتعبير بالماضى فى الموضعين لتحقق الوقوع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the first clause is a curse on the whole person, with “hands” as a metonym or part-for-whole figure; the author answers that whole-person usage is attested.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء الاول دعاء بهلاك جملته على ان اليدين اما كناية عن الذات والنفس لما بينهما من اللزوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The reading transmitted from Ibn Abbas in the Two Sahihs, “and he has indeed perished,” makes the second clause factual, since “qad” does not precede supplication.
rows.anchor: وفى الصحيحين وغيرهما من حديث ابن عباس فى سبب النزول فنزلت هذه السورة تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the first clause as the ruin of Abu Lahab’s work, which did not help him, and the second as the ruin of his person.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاول اخبار عن هلاك عمله حيث لم يفده ولم يمنعه لان الاعمال تزاول بالايدى غالبا والثانى اخبار عن هلاك نفسه

rows.speaker: الماتريدى
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi reads “hands” as favors: Abu Lahab’s favors toward Muhammad and Quraysh were lost through enmity and Quraysh’s defeat, while the second clause predicts his death.
rows.anchor: وفى التأويلات اليد بمعنى النعمة وكان يحسن إلى النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والى قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using Abu Lahab’s kunya publicizes the curse and fixes it as his lasting designation; other proposed motives include avoiding his ugly name, his flaming cheeks, wordplay, or a hell-bound allusion.
rows.anchor: وذكر بكنيته لاشتهاره بها وقد أريد تشهيره بدعوة السوء وان تبقى سمة له وذكره بأشهر علميه أوفق بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rhetorical analysis treats Abu Lahab as an allusion to a person of Hell, since association with flame entails being hellish; scholars dispute whether the kunya’s literal sense is also intended.
rows.anchor: أو لجعله كناية عن الجهنمى فكأنه قيل تبت يدا جهنمى وذلك لان انتسابه إلى اللهب كانتساب الاب إلى الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid’s claim that the kunya functions allusively only because Abu Lahab was famous by that name fails: such inference does not depend on a person’s fame.
rows.anchor: وزعم السيد أيضا ان الكناية فدل أبى لهب لانه اشتهر بهذا الاسم وبكونه جهنميا

rows.speaker: ابن محيص
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Kathir read Abu Lahab with a vowelless hāʾ; al-Zamakhshari calls it alteration of proper names, while Abu al-Baqaʾ regards it as a dialectal variant by the Kufan analysis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيص وابن كثير أبى لهب بسكون الهاء وهو من تغيير الاعلام على مافى الكشاف وقال أبو البقاء الفتح والسكون لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “mā” is usually negative: his wealth did not protect him when ruin arrived; it may instead be interrogative, asking what his wealth accomplished.
rows.anchor: أى لم يغنى عنه ماله حين حل به التباب على أن ما نافية ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What he earned” may be a relative phrase or a verbal noun meaning his earning.
rows.anchor: كسبه على أن ما موصولة وجوز أن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says that if the first “mā” is interrogative, the second may also ask what he earned, implying that he earned nothing.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان اذا كان ما الاولى استفهامية فيجوز أن تكون هذه كذلك أى وأى شىء كسب

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: Issam al-Din offers a negative reading: his wealth did not avert harm, and what he earned brought no benefit; the author objects to making wealth the subject of “earned.”
rows.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن تكون نافية والمعنى ما أغنى عنه ماله مضرة وما كسب منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bahr prefers the relative reading, with an omitted object pronoun: what he gained in profits, benefits, status, and followers.
rows.anchor: واستظهر فى البحر موصوليتها فالعائد محذوف أى والذى كسبه به من الارباح والنتائج والمنافع والوجاهة والاتباع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains what Abu Lahab earned as his evil plotting against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو ماله والذى كسبه من عمله الخبيث الذى هو كيده فى عداوة النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما قال الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets it as deeds he thought valuable but which became worthless, linking the expression to the Quranic image of deeds turned to scattered dust.
rows.anchor: أو من عمله الذى يظن أنه منه على شىء كقوله تعالى وقدمنا إلى ماعملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا كما قال قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say “what he earned” means his children.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ومجاهد ماكسب من الولد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Abu Dawud transmits Aisha’s report that a man’s best food is from his own earnings and his child is part of his earnings.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو داود عن عائشة مرفوعا أن أطيب مايأكل الرجل من كسبه وان ولده من كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab reportedly boasted that he would ransom himself with wealth and children if Muhammad’s claim were true; he had three sons, two of whom accepted Islam at the conquest and were blessed by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه كان كان يقول ان كان مايقول ابن أخى حقا فانا أفتدى منه نفسى بمالى وولدى وكان له ثلاثة أبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His son Utaybah did not convert, divorced Umm Kulthum under his father’s threat, then insulted the Prophet and divorced her himself.
rows.anchor: قال أبو لهب لهما رأسى ورأسكما حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Utaybah announced disbelief in the star and in the one who drew near, spat toward the Prophet without hitting him, and was cursed by the Prophet after threatening him.
rows.anchor: فقال يامحمد انى كافر بالنجم اذا هوى وبالذى دنا فتدلى ثم تفل تجاه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that a beast of prey attack Utaybah; on the journey to Syria a lion singled him out and killed him despite the group’s precautions.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى تعالى عليه وسلم اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: The report’s account of the lion killing Utaybah is followed by a verse attributed to Hassan.
rows.anchor: وفى ذلك يقول حسان من يرجع العام إلى أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab died of al-ʿadasa seven nights after Badr; his family feared contagion, left him three days until he stank, then arranged his burial.
rows.anchor: وهلك أبو لهب نفسه بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر لسبع ليال فاجتنبه أهله مخافة العدوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burial accounts differ: some say hired porters placed him in a dug grave, others that they leaned him against a wall and buried him under stones from a distance.
rows.anchor: فلما خافوا العار استأجروا بعض السودان فاحتملوه ودفنوه وفى رواية حفروا له حفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says events unfolded as the Quran had foretold; Abd Allah’s reading has the intensive form “wa-mā iktasaba.”
rows.anchor: فكان الامر كما أخبر به القرآن وقرأ عبد الله وماأكتسب بناء الافتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means Abu Lahab will certainly enter and suffer Hell; the future particle stresses certainty and the indefinite noun magnifies the fire.
rows.anchor: سيدخاها لامحالة فى الآخرة ويقاسى حرها والسين لتأكيد الوعيد والتنوين للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A fire with flame” describes an intensely blazing and burning fire, namely Hell.
rows.anchor: ذات اشتعال وتوقد عظيم وهى نار جهنم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf reads this as an answer to Abu Lahab’s boast that he could ransom himself, and as mockery of his wealth and sons; this image especially suits “what he earned” as offspring.
rows.anchor: قال فى الكشف استئناف جوابا عما كان يقول انا افتدى بمالى ويتوهم من صدقه وفى تحسير له وتهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another scholar says the first verse indicates the ruin of Abu Lahab’s works and this one his own ruin, depending on the earlier interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الافاضل الاولى اشارة لهلاك عمله وهذه اشارة لهلاك نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife clause is coordinated with the unexpressed subject of “will enter,” separated from it by the object; “carrier of firewood” is accusative as an insult, or circumstantial if the construct is prospective.
rows.anchor: عطف على المستكن فى سيصلى لمكان الفصل بالمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab’s wife was Umm Jamil bint Harb, sister of Abu Sufyan.
rows.anchor: وهى أم جميل بنت حرب أخت أبى سفيان

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: A report via Ja'far al-Sadiq and his father describes Aqil telling Muawiya that Abu Lahab lies in Hell with his aunt beneath him; the author doubts its attribution to al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: اخرج ابن عساكر عن جعفر الصادق عن أبيه محمد الباقر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن عقيل بن أبى طالب دخل على معاوية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says she brought thorn branches at night and scattered them in the Prophet’s path.
rows.anchor: على ماأخرج بن أبى حاتم وابن جرير عن ابن زيد كانت تأتى بأغصان الشوك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that despite her wealth she carried firewood on her back from extreme miserliness, making the phrase an insult to her greed.
rows.anchor: وروى عن قتادة أنها مع كثرة مالها كانت نحمل الحطب عالى ظهرها لشدة بخلها فعيرت بالبخل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدى
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi interpret carrying firewood as spreading malicious gossip that kindles hostility among people.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبى حاتم عنه وعن مجاهد انها كانت تمشى بالنميمة وأخرجه ابن أبى حاتم عن الحسن أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Firewood” is a familiar metaphor for gossip, which inflames social discord; describing it as wet wood intensifies the smoke and evil.
rows.anchor: فالحطب مستعار للنميمة وهى استعارة مشهورة ومن ذلك قوله من البيض لم تصطد على ظهر لامة

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says she carries sins and transgressions, with firewood standing metaphorically for sins because both cause burning.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير حمالة الخطايا واذنوب من فلان يحطب على ظهره اذا كان يكتسب الآثام والخطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that “firewood” means the perpetrators whom she induces to sin is a remote grammatical interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحطب جمع حاطب جمع حارس وحرس أى تحمل الجناة على الجنايات وهومحمل بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings vary in the verb, the diminutive and hamza of “his wife,” and the case or annexation of “carrier of firewood”; most read it nominatively in construct, with other nominative or accusative forms.
rows.anchor: وقر أبو حيوة وابن مقسم سيصلى بضم الياء وفتح الصاد وشد اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “on her neck is a rope” has several parses: a circumstantial nominal clause related to the carrier or wife, a predicate, or a second predicate, with different analyses for “rope.”
rows.anchor: جملة من خبر مقدم ومبتدأ مؤخر فى موضع الحال من الضمير فى حمالة وقيل من أمرأته المعطوف على الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Al-Masad is anything tightly twisted into rope, such as palm fiber according to Abu al-Fath; others say any fiber, Yemeni tree bark, camel hide, or camel hair.
rows.anchor: والمسد مامسد أى فتل من الحبال فتلا شديدا من ليف المقل على ماقال أبو الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rope pictures her as a wood-carrier who ties the bundle around her neck, degrading her and her husband despite their wealth and status.
rows.anchor: والمراد تصويرها بصورة الحطابة التى تحمل الحزمة وتربطها فى جيدها تخسيسا لحالها وتحقيرا لها

rows.speaker: الفضل بن العباس
rows.claim: Al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas ibn Utbah defended his lineage in a poem when people mocked him as descended from a firewood-carrier.
rows.anchor: ولقد عير بغض الناس الفضل بن العباس بن عتبة بن أبى لهب بحاله الحطب فقال مذا أردت إلى شتمى ومنقصتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When she heard the surah, she reportedly went to Abu Bakr with a pestle and threatened the Prophet, calling him a poet and quoting a counter-verse.
rows.anchor: وقد أغضبها ذلك فيروى أنها لما سمعت السورة أتت أبا بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Umm Jamil could not see the Prophet though Abu Bakr was beside him; the Prophet said angels had screened him and God protected him from her.
rows.anchor: وأمره عصينا وأعمى الله تعالى بصرها عن رسول الله صلى تعالى عليه وسلم فروى أن أبا بكر قال لها هل ترى معى أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of her blindness may reinforce the metaphor in “carrier of firewood.”
rows.anchor: وقيل ان ذلك ترشيح للمجاز بناء على اعتباره فى حمالة الحطب

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests an afterlife image: she carries a bundle of firewood from the Zaqqum or Dari tree, with a rope of fire replacing her noose; sinners are punished in kind.
rows.anchor: وفى الكشاف يحتمل أن يكون المعنى تكون فى نار جهنم على الصورة التى كانت عليها حين كانت تحمل حزمة الشوك

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير ومجاهد وسفيان
rows.claim: The hellfire image is transmitted from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and Sufyan; the rope is interpreted as a chain of fire.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا عن عروة بن الزبير ومجاهد وسفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax changes with the accusative or nominative reading of “carrier of firewood”: it may be circumstantial with the rope clause, or a description explaining her burning.
rows.anchor: وأمر الاعراب على مافى الكشف انه أن نصب حمالة يكون حالا هو والجملة أعنى فى جيدها حبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses “jīd,” a word associated with jewelry, rather than “neck,” commonly paired with shackles and humiliation, creating pointed irony.
rows.anchor: انما لم يقل سبحانه فى عنقها والمعروف أن يذكر العنق مع الغل ونحوه مما فيه امتهان كما قال تعالى فى اعناقهم أغلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rhetorical explanation says “his wife” rather than “his spouse” taunts her; the wording may conflict with the Quran’s description of Abraham’s wife standing by.
rows.anchor: قيل امرأته ولم يقل زوجه انتهى وهو بديع جدا الا انه يعكر على آخره قوله تعالى وامرأته قائمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says her necklace was of shells; al-Hasan says beads, while Ibn al-Musayyib says it was an expensive jeweled necklace.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة انه كان فى جيدها قلادة من ودع وفى معناه قول الحسن من خرز وقال ابن المسيب كانت قلادة فاخرة من جوهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She vowed to spend her necklace against Muhammad; on this reading, an iron rope in Hell replaces her jewel, while the shell reading underlines her miserliness.
rows.anchor: وأنها قالت واللات والعزى لانفقنها على عداوة محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ولعل المراد على هذا انها تكون في نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the verse as a curse that she be strangled by a rope, citing a report she died that way while carrying wood; the author says this does not require that interpretation.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الكلام يحتمل أن يكون دعاء عليها بالخنق بالحبل وهو عن الذهن مناط الثريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theological debate asks how Abu Lahab could be commanded to believe when the prediction that he will burn entails he will remain an unbeliever, seemingly requiring him to believe the contradictory claim that he will not believe.
rows.anchor: واستشكل أمر تكليف أبى لهب بالايمان مع قوله تعالى سيصلى الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says he must believe the Prophet’s whole message in general, not every Quranic detail, so he need not believe the prediction about his own continued unbelief.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن ماكلفه هو الايمان بجميع ماجاء به النبى عليه الصلاة والسلام اجمالا لا الايمان بتفاصيل مانطق به القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer says the threat of Hell does not prove unbelief, since a sinner may enter for wrongdoing; this response does not work for the unbelievers addressed in al-Kafirun.
rows.anchor: بأن قوله تعالى سيصلى الخ ليس نصا فى أنه لايؤمن أصلا فان صلى النار غير مختص بالكفار

rows.speaker: الكعبى وأبو الحسين البصرى والقاضى عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi, Abu al-Husayn al-Basri, and Qadi Abd al-Jabbar offer another answer, which the Imam rejects; the argument is deferred to longer theological works.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الكعبى وأبو الحسين البصرى وكذا القاضى عبد الجبار بغير ماذكر مما رده الامام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further answer makes the threat conditional: he will burn if he dies without believing, so it does not explicitly say he will never believe.
rows.anchor: وقيل فى خصوص هذه الآية أن المعنى سيصلى نارا ذات لهب ويخلد فيها ان مات ولم يؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Abu Lahab’s wife is cited as evidence that unbelievers may validly marry one another.
rows.anchor: واستدل بقوله تعالى وامراته على صحة أنكحة الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Ikhlas is named for its monotheism and called the Foundation because it grounds the other principles of religion.
rows.anchor: وسميت بها لما فيها من التوحيد ولذا سميت أيضا بالاساس أصل لسائر أصول الدين

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A report attributed to Kaʿb says the seven heavens and earths were founded upon this surah; its meaning is that creation points to God’s unity and attributes, though the report is not in recognized hadith collections.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب كما قال الجاحظ بن رجب أسست السموات السبع والارضون السبع على هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says creation is founded upon truth, justice, and monotheism, while a further argument makes divine unity the condition for the possible existence of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: ماخلقناهما الا بالحق وهو العدل والتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed proof says God’s unity makes the heavens and earth possible by excluding rival gods and mutual obstruction.
rows.anchor: مصحح ايجادهما أى بعد امكانهما الذاتى ما أشارت اليه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is also called al-Muqashqisha, Tawhid, Tafrid, Tajrid, Najat, Wilaya, and Maʿrifa because its contents teach knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: والمقشقشة لما سمعت فى تفسير سورة الكافرون وسورة التوحيد وسورة التفريد وسورة التجريد وسورة النجاة وسورة الولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called Beauty based on a report about God loving beauty, but the author doubts the report’s authenticity.
rows.anchor: وسورة الجمال قيل لما روى انه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال ان الله جميل يحب الجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Attribution because it answers a request to describe God; a separate report from Abu Hurayra is called extremely weak and even fabricated in al-Mizan.
rows.anchor: وسورة النسبة لورودها جوابا لمن قال انسب لنا ربك على ماستسمعه ان شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أنيس
rows.claim: A sound-chain report says the Prophet taught Ibn Unays to recite Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas as refuge, and that no one seeks refuge with their equal.
rows.anchor: ما أخرج النسائى والبزار وابن مردويه بسند صحيح عن عبد الله بن أنيس قال أن رسول الله صالى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وضع يده على صدرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a worshipper recited this surah and the Prophet called him a servant who knew his Lord.
rows.anchor: وفى اثر أن رجلا صلى فقرأها فقال النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ان هذا عبد عرف ربه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The name al-Maniʿa is introduced through a report from Ibn Abbas about the surah’s protective merit.
rows.anchor: وسورة المانعة قيل لما روى ابن عباس أنه تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says that during the ascension God gave the Prophet al-Ikhlas from the treasures of the Throne as protection from grave distress and the fires.
rows.anchor: قال لنبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم حين عرج به أعطيتك سورة الاخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards this protective report as apparently unsound; it conflicts with Abu Umama’s report of four verses from the heavenly treasury.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عدم صحة هذا الخبر ويعارضه ماأخرجه ابن الضريس عن أبى أمامة

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that four verses came from the heavenly treasury: the Opening, the Throne Verse, the end of al-Baqara, and al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: أربع آيات نزلت من كنز العرش لم ينزل منه غيرهن أم الكتاب وآية الكرسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other names are based on claims that angels gather to hear the surah and Satan flees it.
rows.anchor: وسورة المحضر قيل لان الملائكة عليهم السلام تحضر لاستماعها اذا قرئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baraʾa is attributed to a report in which the Prophet says a reciter is free of polytheism; the author does not know its transmitter.
rows.anchor: وسورة البراءة قيل لما روى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام رأى رجلا يقروها

rows.speaker: مهاجر
rows.claim: Abu Nuʿaym transmits from Muhajir that the Prophet said a reader of al-Kafirun was free from shirk and a reader of Ikhlas was forgiven.
rows.anchor: نعم روى أبو نعم من طريق عمرو بن مرزوق عن شعبة عن مهاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers deriving the name al-Baraʾa from the report that reading Ikhlas one hundred times at bedtime brings release from Hellfire.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاولى أن يقال سميت بذلك لما فى حديث الترمذى عن أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is also called the Reminder of pure monotheism, the Light, and Faith because its teaching is necessary to complete faith.
rows.anchor: وهى مكية فى قول عبد الله والحسن عكرمة وعطاء ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن كعب وأبو العالية والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Abu al-Aliya, and al-Dahhak hold that the surah is Medinan.
rows.anchor: مدنية فى قول ابن عباس ومحمد ابن كعب وأبى العالية والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If sound, Ibn Abbas’s earlier report supports a Meccan origin; al-Itqan notes two conflicting occasion reports, reconciled by some as repeated revelation, while its author leans Medinan.
rows.anchor: وخبر ابن عباس السابق ان صح ظاهر فى انها عنده مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dawani’s claim that the surah is Meccan by consensus reveals poor familiarity with the disagreement.
rows.anchor: وعلى مافى الكتابين لايخفى مافى قول الدوانى انها مكية بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has five verses in Meccan and Syrian counting, and four in other systems.
rows.anchor: وآيها خمس فى المكى والشامى أربع فى غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement after al-Masad is attributed either to matching sound endings, or preferably to its semantic continuation of al-Kafirun: together they express negation and affirmation of monotheism.
rows.anchor: وقيل وهو الاولى انها متصلة بقل ياأيها الكافرون فى المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars pair the two surahs in several prayers; their separation here has an earlier rationale, and placing Ikhlas after al-Masad also answers Abu Lahab specifically.
rows.anchor: ولذا يسميان المقشقشتين وقرن بينهما فى القراءة فى صلوات كثيرة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Mubarak ibn Fadala transmits from Anas that the Prophet promised Paradise to a man who loved this surah; Ahmad records it and al-Bukhari cites it without a full chain.
rows.anchor: وروى مبارك بن فضالة عن أنس ان لرجلا قال يارسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Malik transmits from Abu Hurayra that a man’s recitation made Paradise obligatory; al-Nasaʾi and al-Tirmidhi report it, and al-Tirmidhi calls it sound but known only through Malik.
rows.anchor: وروى مالك عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن قال سمعت أبا هريرة

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: A hasan-garib report says a supplication invoking God as the One and Self-Sufficient uses His Greatest Name, by which He answers requests.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو داود وابن ماجه والترمذى وقال حسن غريب عن بريدة

rows.speaker: محجن بن الأدرع
rows.claim: In the Musnad, the Prophet hears Mahjan invoke the One and Self-Sufficient after prayer and says three times that he has been forgiven.
rows.anchor: وفى المسند عن محجن بن الادرع ان النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم دخل المسجد

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari and other collections says a man repeatedly recited Ikhlas; the Prophet affirmed that it equals one-third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البخارى ومالك وأبو داود والنسائى عن أبى سعيد

rows.speaker: أبى بن كعب
rows.claim: Ahmad and al-Nasaʾi transmit a report from Ubayy or an Ansari that reciting the surah equals reciting one-third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والنسائى فى اليوم والليلة من طريق هشيم عن ابى بن كعب

rows.speaker: يوسف بن عطية الصفار
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ubayy promises the reward of reciting one-third of the Quran and good deeds corresponding to those who associated partners with God and believed.
rows.anchor: وفى رواية يوسف بن عطية الصفار بسنده عن أبى مرفوعا من قرأقا هو الله أحد فكانما قرأ ثلث القرآن

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: A report via Ibn Lahia says Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman spent the night reciting Ikhlas; the Prophet said it equaled half or one-third of the Quran, with other reports resolving the uncertainty as one-third.
rows.anchor: وفى المسند من طريق ابن لهيعة عن عن احرث بن يزيد عن أبى الهيثم عن أبى سعيد قال بات قتادة بن النعمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the surah’s subject is one of three Quranic parts, not that its recitation earns one-third the reward of the whole.
rows.anchor: واختلف فى المراد بذلك فقيل المراد أنها باعتبار معناها ثلث من القرآن المجزأ إلى ثلاثة لا أن ثواب قراءتها ثلث ثواب القرآن

rows.speaker: الغزالى
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali identifies the Quran’s three knowledge types as knowledge of origin, return, and the path between them; Ikhlas addresses the first.
rows.anchor: وقال تالغزالى في الجواهر ماحاصله هى عدل ثلثه

rows.speaker: الجوينى
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni says Quranic essentials are knowledge of God, belief in His Messenger, and belief in standing before Him; Ikhlas supplies the first, making it one-third on that basis.
rows.anchor: وقال الجونى المطالب التى فى القرآن معظمها الاصول الثلاثة اتى بها يصح الاسلام ويحصل الايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other schemes divide the Quran into narratives, rulings, and beliefs, or into reports about Creator, creation, and commands; Ikhlas focuses exclusively on its report about the Creator.
rows.anchor: وقيل القرآن قسمان خبر وانشاء والخبر قسمان خبر عن الخالق وخبر عن المخلوق فهذه ثلاثة أثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one-third and whole-Quran equivalence reports can coexist if the Quran’s ultimate purpose is monotheism and its other subjects are means, assuming the whole-Quran report is sound.
rows.anchor: وأياما كان قيل لاتنافى بين رواية الثلث

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A sound Muslim report says God divided the Quran into three portions and this surah is one portion, supporting substantive partition rather than a reward ratio.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد اعتبار الاجزاء انفسها دون الثواب ما فى صحيح مسلم من طريق قتادة عن أبى الدرداء

rows.speaker: ابن عقيل
rows.claim: Ibn Aqil rejects the reward-equivalence reading: ten rewards per Quranic letter would make the whole Quran’s reward vastly larger than this short surah.
rows.anchor: وضعف ذلك ابن عقيل وقال لايجوز أن يكون المعنى فله أجر ثلث القرآن لقوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من قرأ القرآن فله بكل حرف عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: الدوانى
rows.claim: Al-Dawani answers that readers receive detailed reward per letter and a separate general reward for completing the Quran; Ikhlas may equal one-third of the latter.
rows.anchor: والدوانى أورد هذا اشكالا على هذا القول ثم أجاب بان للقارىء ثوابين تفصيليا بحسب قلراءة الحروف واجماليا بسب ختمه القرآن

rows.speaker: الكرمانى
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani’s analogy distinguishes the baseline reward of reciting one instance of the surah from extra reward for the greater effort of reading a third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وفى شرح البخارى للكرمانى فان قلت المشقة فى قراءة الثلث أكثر منها فى قراءتها

rows.speaker: الخفاجى
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji argues that thoughtful, correctly performed recitation with understanding can equal the reward of a third of the Quran recited without reflection, or of a third lacking material on knowing God.
rows.anchor: والذى عندى فى ذلك ان للنظر فى معنى كلام الله تعالى المتدبر لآياته ثوابا وللتالى له وان لم يفهمه ثواب آخر

rows.speaker: الخفاجى
rows.claim: He compares the surah’s precious meanings combined with precious wording to a jewel-inlaid gold tablet worth more than its weight in plain gold.
rows.anchor: ولابدع فى أشرف المعنى اذا ضم لبعض من أشرف الالفاظ أن يعدل من جنس تلك الالفاظ مقدارا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds al-Khafaji’s answer no more convincing than earlier explanations.
rows.anchor: ولاأرى له كثير امتياز على غيره مما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s answer is that God may multiply the reward for an easy act beyond that of harder acts; His generosity is unlimited, so the precise reason can remain among matters known only to Him.
rows.anchor: لامانع من ان يخص الله عز وجل بعض العبادات التى ليس فيها كثير مشقة بثواب اكثر من ثواب ماهو جنسها واشق منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation resembles the special multiplied merit of particular times and places, and does not exceed the mystery of why worship is obligatory in some periods and forbidden in others.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بابعد ولاأبدع من تخصيص بعض الازمنة والامكنة الماهية بان للعبادة منه ولو قليلة من الثواب

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says silence on this question is preferable and safer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عبد البر السكوت فى هذه المسئلة أفضل من الكلام فيها وأسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening report from Muawiya ibn Muawiya al-Laythi has only weak chains; sound reports suffice for the surah’s virtue, and some call it the Quran’s best surah.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حديث معاوية بن معاوية الليثى الذى افتتح به الامام الكلام فى هذه السورة الكريمة خرجه الطبرانى وأبو يعلى من طرق كلها ضعيفة

rows.speaker: صفوان الكلاعى
rows.claim: A report in al-Darimi says the Prophet called Ikhlas the greatest surah, though this does not prove it is absolutely the best.
rows.anchor: بل قيل لذلك انها أفضل سورة فى القرآن ومنهم من استدل عليه بما روى الدارمى فى مسنده عن أبى المغيرة عن صفوان الكلاعى

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet taught Uqba three of the best surahs revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran: Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas; al-Tirmidhi grades a version hasan.
rows.anchor: وفى المسند من طريقى معاذ بن رفاعة وأسيد بن عبد الرحمن عن عقبة بن عامر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم الا أعلمك خير ثلاث سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports establish that Ikhlas is among the best surahs, not that it is absolutely the best; Ibn al-Hassad marvels that disagreement persists despite abundant preference reports.
rows.anchor: وروى الترمذى بعض هذا الحديث وحسنه ولايدل على أنها أفضل سور القرآن مطلقا بل على أنها من الافضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say surah preference reflects multiplied reward through the reader’s contemplation and reverence; others say it reflects the superior meanings in the wording itself.
rows.anchor: واختلف القائلون بالتفضيل فقال بعضهم الفضل راجع إلى عظم ومضاعفة الثواب بحسب انتقالات النفس وخشيتها

rows.speaker: الحليمى
rows.claim: Al-Halimi, transmitting from al-Bayhaqi, offers several senses of preference: practical usefulness, inclusion of divine names and attributes, immediate protective benefit and worship, or specially multiplied reward by divine choice.
rows.anchor: ونقل الحليمى عن البيهقى ان معنى التفضيل بين الآيات والسور يرجع إلى أشياء أحدها أن يكون العمل بها أولى من العمل باخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preference on any of these grounds does not conflict with every surah being God’s word and equally attributable to Him.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة التفضيل باحد هذه الاعتبارات لاينافى كون الكل كلام الله عز وجل ومتحد النسبة اليه سبحانه
